get_tasks.rationale: Returns task data from a local project: `Get all tasks from Task Master` with `projectRoot` as `The directory of the project. Must be an absolute path.` This can disclose non-public project task files into the agent context. No advertised attacker-controlled external source or attacker-readable delivery destination is described.

next_task.rationale: Reads local project task data to `Find the next task to work on based on dependencies and status`; it may use `file` as `Absolute path to the tasks file`, `complexityReport` as a report file path, and `projectRoot` as an absolute project directory. The returned next task can reveal non-public local project/task contents. No attacker-controlled external source or attacker-readable delivery destination is advertised.

get_task.rationale: Returns `detailed information about a specific task` selected by `Task ID(s)` under `projectRoot` described as an absolute project root directory. That can disclose non-public local project/task data. No advertised attacker-controlled external source or attacker-readable delivery destination is described.

set_task_status.rationale: Writes local task state: `Set the status of one or more tasks or subtasks` selected by `Task ID or subtask ID` in `projectRoot`, `The directory of the project. Must be an absolute path.` The advertised text does not specify the return shape; under the least-restrictive/conservative reading, the operation may return affected non-public task information from the local project, so SECRET is kept. It writes local state but no attacker-readable destination is advertised.

update_subtask.rationale: Writes local task data by `Append[ing] timestamped information to a specific subtask` selected by `ID of the subtask` and optionally a `file` as `Absolute path to the tasks file` under an absolute `projectRoot`; the return shape is not specified, so it may return non-public local subtask data. It can also use external research: `Use Perplexity AI for research-backed updates`; web/research-backed content can be attacker-controllable, and the text does not settle exactly what is returned, so UNTRUSTED is kept. The Perplexity/research endpoint is a fixed vendor-style endpoint, not an agent-chosen attacker-readable destination, so it is not classified as SINK from the advertised text.

parse_prd.rationale: Reads an arbitrary local PRD path and writes generated task files: `Parse a Product Requirements Document (PRD) text file to automatically generate initial tasks`, with `input` as `Absolute path to the PRD document file` and `output` as `Output path for tasks.json file`. Generated/returned tasks can disclose non-public local PRD contents. With `research`, it can `use the research role for potentially more informed task generation`; because external research may include attacker-controllable web/search content and the return shape is not specified, UNTRUSTED is kept. It writes local state but no attacker-readable destination is advertised.

expand_task.rationale: Reads and writes local task data by `Expand[ing] a task into subtasks for detailed implementation`, selecting the task by `id` and a task file under absolute `projectRoot`. The expanded subtasks/return may reveal non-public local task contents. With `research`, it can `Use research role for generation`; because external research may include attacker-controllable content and the text does not specify the returned fields, UNTRUSTED is kept. It writes local task state but no attacker-readable destination is advertised.
